'''Melanie Becker''' (1966–2020) was a German-American physicist known for her research into [[string theory]]. She was a tenured professor of physics at [[Texas A&M University]].

== Early life and education ==
Melanie Becker was originally from Germany but grew up in [[Málaga|Malaga]], Spain where she graduated from Instituto Nacional de Enseñanza Mixto de Torremolinos in 1987.<ref name=":1" /> She received her [[Diplom]] in physics focusing on String Theory from the [[University of Bonn]] in 1994 <ref>{{Cite web |title=Melanie Becker |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/melanie-becker |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University |language=en}}</ref> while working with [[Werner Nahm]]. She simultaneously worked with [[Luis Álvarez-Gaumé]] at the particle accelerator at [[CERN]] when earning her [[Diplom]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Melanie Becker |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/melanie-becker |access-date=2022-06-30 |website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University |language=en}}</ref> Following her [[Doctorate|Ph.D]], Melanie Becker was in California first as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] until 1997, when she transitioned to the [[California Institute of Technology]] as a senior research fellow working with [[John Henry Schwarz|John H. Schwarz]]. In 2000 she moved to the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] as an assistant professor marking the start of her independent academic career. In 2005 she moved to [[Texas A&M University]] where she was given tenure on arrival and became a member of the George P. and Cynthia Woods Michell Institute for Fundamental Physics and Astronomy.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Becker's research centered on the study of gravity and similar theories, with a particulate interest in [[string theory]], [[M-theory]], and [[quantum gravity]]. Becker's work included developing models for [[Superstring theory|superstring compactification]] and, working with her sister [[Katrin Becker]], she developed one for the [[Kaluza–Klein theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Becker |first1=Katrin |last2=Becker |first2=Melanie |last3=Robbins |first3=Daniel |date=2015 |title=Kaluza-Klein theories without truncation |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/JHEP02(2015)140 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2015 |issue=2 |page=140 |doi=10.1007/JHEP02(2015)140 |arxiv=1412.8198 |bibcode=2015JHEP...02..140B |s2cid=53471453 |issn=1029-8479}}</ref>

As she accepted her position to be a professor of physics at Texas A&M in 2005, Melanie was given the opportunity to work alongside her sister, [[Katrin Becker]], to further their studies and specialization in string theory. In general, the models that Melanie developed compared the outcomes from standard elementary particle physics and cosmology.
<ref name=mt>{{cite web |last1=Tresaugue |first1=Matthew |title=Texas A&M using new methods to add faculty |url=https://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/article/Texas-A-M-using-new-methods-to-add-faculty-1889029.php |website=Chron |publisher=The Houston Chronicle |access-date=31 October 2023}}</ref>

Being distinguished as a Harvard Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study Science Fellow in 2005, Becker focused her work during her time here on developing models from string theory that could reproduce experimental data measured within particle accelerators in relation to cosmological data. This stems from her graduate research conducted at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN), where the models studied are known as "compactifications of string theory on manifolds with torsion."
<ref>{{cite web |title=Melanie Becker |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/melanie-becker |website=Harvard Radcliffe Institute |access-date=31 October 2023}}</ref>

In 2006 Becker, her sister [[Katrin Becker]], and John Schwartz published a graduate-level textbook on string theory and M-theory.<ref>Review for ''String theory and M-theory''
*{{Cite journal |last=Ramond |first=Pierre |date=2008 |title=String Theory and M-Theory: A Modern Introduction String Theory and M-Theory: A Modern Introduction: Katrin Becker, Melanie Becker, and John H. Schwarz, Cambridge U. Press, New York, 2007. $80.00 (739 pp.). ISBN 978-0-521-86069-7 |url=http://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.2930740 |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=61 |issue=5 |page=57 |doi=10.1063/1.2930740 |issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Hosted by the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], Becker was invited as a lecturer for their 2010 Prospects in Theoretical Physics (PiTP) program titled ''Aspects of Supersymmetry''.
<ref>{{cite web |title=PiTP "Aspects of Supersymmetry" |url=https://static.ias.edu/pitp/archive/index2010_final.html}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Melanie Becker was born to Ingrid and Karl-Hans Becker in [[Ahaus]], Germany, on 12 August 1966. She grew up in Malaga, Spain, with her younger sister [[Katrin Becker]]. Becker and her younger sister moved to [[College Station, Texas|College Station]] and were recruited to Texas A&M in 2005 as part of a faculty reinvestment program. She lived there for the rest of her life.<ref name=mt/> Melanie Becker died on 13 March 2020 at the age of 53, after a year-long fight with cancer.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2020-03-18 |title=Texas A&M Mourns Loss of Physicist and String Theorist Melanie Becker |url=https://science.tamu.edu/news/2020/03/texas-am-mourns-loss-of-physicist-and-string-theorist-melanie-becker/ |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Texas A&M College of Science |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hutchins |first=Shana K. |date=2020-03-20 |title=Melanie Becker |url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.6.4o.20200320a/full |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=2020 |issue=4o |article-number=0320a |doi=10.1063/PT.6.4o.20200320a|bibcode=2020PhT..2020....4. |s2cid=242929335 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name= ":2">{{Cite web |date=2020-03-13 |title=Dr. Melanie Becker Obituary 2020 |url=https://www.hillierfuneralhome.com/obituaries/dr-melaniebecker |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=Hillier Funeral Home and Cremations |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2001 Becker received a fellowship from the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref name=":0" /> 
In 2004 she received a fellowship from the Research Internships in Science and Engineering (RISE) for the development of string theory among young undergraduate female students.
In 2005 she received the Edward, Frances and Shirley B. Daniels fellowship from the Harvard Radcliffe Institute.
<ref name=":0" />
